title: Croque Monsieur
subtitle: French toasted ham and Gruyère sandwich with béchamel
excerpt: The great French café sandwich: toasted bread filled with ham and Gruyère, spread with béchamel inside and on top, then grilled until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is browned and blistered.

recipe.sourceNotes: Croque monsieur (literally 'mister crunch') is one of the iconic dishes of Parisian café culture, appearing on menus across France and served from breakfast through to late evening. The sandwich consists of sliced bread (typically brioche or pain de mie) filled with good-quality cooked ham and Gruyère, spread with béchamel sauce, topped with more Gruyère, and grilled until golden. The béchamel is not optional; its role is to create a creamy, savoury sauce that holds the sandwich together and becomes the defining flavour element when browned under the grill. A croque madame is the same sandwich with a fried egg placed on top. The quality of the ham and cheese determines the quality of the finished croque.

content.text: The béchamel should be thick enough to hold its shape on the bread rather than running off. It is spread inside the sandwich as well as on top; this prevents the bread from drying out during grilling and adds flavour throughout. Use a very hot grill and watch closely; the topping can go from golden to burnt very quickly.

items.preparation: thick slices; or brioche or pain de mie

content.text: Make the béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour, cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until thick. Season. Stir in the mustard and a quarter of the cheese.
Toast the bread lightly. Spread béchamel on one side of each slice. Layer ham and half the remaining cheese on 2 slices. Top with the other slices, béchamel side in.

Spread the remaining béchamel on top of each sandwich and scatter with the last of the Gruyère. Grill under a very hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Serve immediately.
